title: Taiwan’s Tech Diplomacy Has a Labor Problem
gist: A Transparentem investigation found migrant workers at Taiwanese electronics manufacturers paying about $6,400 in recruitment fees, including at Garmin and Compal suppliers, with firms reimbursing only current workers. Short excerpt.

themes.theme: Migrant labor in Taiwan electronics supply chains

insights.claim: Transparentem interviewed 24 workers at seven manufacturers in Taiwan and documented recruitment fees totaling $6,400 each, with three Garmin factory workers saying recruiters forced them to sign documents falsely denying the fees.
insights.speaker: Ethan Chiu
insights.so_what: Forced-labor and recruitment-fee exposure is a supply-chain ESG and regulatory risk for US electronics brands.

insights.claim: Compal and Garmin said they had long prohibited worker-paid fees but reimbursed only current migrant workers after investigators made contact and excluded former workers, indicating policies were not enforced.
insights.speaker: Ethan Chiu
insights.so_what: Gap between stated policies and practice raises reputational and compliance risk.
